outcome: hypotension (systolic blood pressure reduction >30% from baseline)
cohort: 722 parturient undergoing cesarean section under spinal anesthesia.
finding: The risk of hypotension following spinal anesthesia for cesarean section significantly increased with estimated blood loss exceeding 500 mL and when the sensory block level rose above T4, while the use of 0.2 mg intrathecal morphine was associated with a higher incidence of bradycardia.
cross-section timing: during and immediately following spinal anesthesia for cesarean section
